jobs.description: 293529183 PURPOSE OF THIS POSITION To communicate with patients and provide administrative support for the practice. Blanchard Valley Health System-Mission, Vision and Values: Mission: Caring for a lifetime. Vision: Extraordinary people. Exceptional care. JOB DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES Duty 1: Schedule and manage patient appointments using Electronic Medical Records (EMR). Manage the Provider's daily patient schedule. Duty 2: Accurately complete the registration process. Duty 3: Document management, patient referrals, prior authorizations and validation of benefits. Duty 4: Responsible for payment collection. Duty 5: Open and set up the office for the day. Stock office supplies. Duty 6: Maintain patient waiting area for cleanliness. Duty 7: Responsible for enhancing our patients experience and upholding the mission, vision and values of the organization. Duty 8: Willingness to participate in process improvement. Duty 9: Other duties as assigned. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS * High school graduate or GED equivalent. * Use of technology, associated applications and office equipment. * This position may not be inclusive to the BVMP Practice that you are assigned at the time of hire, which may require you to work at another BVMP Practice, as needed. * Positive service-oriented interpersonal and communication skills * Behavior needs to adhere to BVHS policies regarding workplace civility and standards of behavior. * Comply to all organizational privacy policies and procedures. * Individual must be able to demonstrate the knowledge and skills necessary to provide care appropriate to the age of the patient served on his/her assigned unit/department. Must be able to interpret the appropriate information needed to identify each patient's requirements relative to their age-specific needs and to provide the care needed as described in the area's policies and procedures. jobs.title: Plant Human Resources Manager
jobs.description: 88393910 293530027 Description Job Plant Human Resources Manager Locations Supported: On-site: Franklin Furnace, Ohio and Ceredo/Quincy, West Virginia (candidate should be local to one of the locations) Reports To: Vice President, Human Resources Direct Reports: None Travel: Up to 30% Position Summary The Plant Human Resources Manager serves as the primary HR Business Partner for two unionized manufacturing sites in Franklin Furnace, Ohio and Ceredo, West Virginia. This role partners closely with plant, operations, and functional leaders to support business priorities, strengthen leadership capability, and deliver practical HR solutions across the full employee lifecycle. The successful incumbent will be a visible, trusted, and highly responsive HR leader who builds credibility with plant leadership, union leadership, and employees by being present in the operation, following through on commitments, communicating clearly, and resolving issues with fairness and practical judgment. This individual will be responsible for all union relations at their sites, including managing communications with union leadership, administering grievances, supporting negotiations, and fostering productive labormanagement relationships. They will be comfortable moving between strategic priorities and daily plant needs, bringing a steady, solutionsoriented approach to complex employee relations, labor relations, compliance, and workforce matters. Key Responsibilities Site Visibility: Maintain regular visibility across assigned sites by spending time with leaders and employees in the plant environment, identifying emerging concerns, reinforcing expectations, and building trust through consistent followup. HR Business Partnership: Serve as the primary HR Business Partner and HR contact for assigned sites, providing practical guidance to plant leadership teams, frontline leaders, and employees across the full employee lifecycle. Core HR Process Leadership: Lead workforce planning, recruitment and selection support, onboarding, retention, performance management, employee development, succession planning, offboarding, employee relations, and change management. Organizational Health: Partner with plant, operations, and functional leaders to assess organizational health, identify talent gaps and workforce risks, strengthen accountability, and implement HR plans that support operational priorities. Employee Relations Management: Manage employee relations matters, including investigations, corrective action, complaints, performance concerns, workplace issues, and documentation, with fairness, urgency, discretion, and sound judgment. Leader Coaching: Coach leaders on communication, documentation, policy and contract application, performance management, leadership effectiveness, employee development, training needs, and succession planning. Union Relations Leadership: Serve as the primary HR lead for all union relations at assigned sites, including managing communications with union leadership, administering and supporting collective bargaining agreements, handling grievances, participating in negotiations, and strengthening collaborative labormanagement relationships that support early issue resolution. CrossFunctional Partnership: Partner with payroll, benefits, compensation, safety, legal, and other functional teams to resolve employee matters and ensure accurate, timely execution of HR processes. HR Systems & Compliance: Support standardized HR systems, processes, practices, job descriptions, compliance training, open enrollment coordination, and workplace investigations in partnership with Corporate HR and the SunCoke Energy Compliance Team. DataDriven Insights: Use HR data, employee feedback, site observations, and business insights to identify trends, evaluate risks, improve processes, and recommend practical solutions that strengthen consistency, compliance, and the employee experience. Other Duties: Lead or support other projects and duties as assigned. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business, Labor Relations, or a related field preferred; equivalent job-related experience will be considered. Approximately 7-10 years of progressive HR experience, including significant HR Business Partner experience and at least 5 years of leadership experience in a unionized manufacturing, industrial, operations, or similarly fast-paced environment. Strong labor and employee relations experience, including collective bargaining agreement administration, grievances, investigations, corrective action, documentation, leader coaching, and resolution of complex workplace matters. Strong working knowledge of applicable employment laws and regulations, including FMLA, ADA, Title VII, wage and hour requirements, and federal, state, and local employment compliance obligations. Demonstrated ability to manage the full employee lifecycle, implement training and leadership development programs, support workforce planning and succession planning, and connect HR priorities to operational performance and business outcomes. Proven ability to build credibility, influence effectively, challenge constructively, coach leaders at multiple levels, and operate with professionalism, discretion, integrity, and sound judgment. Strong organizational, project management, problem-solving, verbal communication, and written communication skills, with high ownership, attention to detail, follow-through, and the ability to operate with urgency in a fast-paced, multi-site environment. Preferred qualifications include experience supporting multi-site unionized manufacturing operations, and experience supporting growth, transformation, integration, or significant operational change. Work Environment This is an on-site position requiring the Plant Human Resources Manager to work on site five days per week. The role will support two manufacturing locations and requires regular presence across Franklin Furnace, Ohio and Ceredo, West Virginia/Quincy, West Virginia. The work environment is fast-paced and operationally focused. The successful candidate must be comfortable spending time in plant environments, partnering closely with site leadership, engaging with employees, and addressing HR matters in real time. Compensation and Benefits The anticipated base salary range for this position is $116,000 - $145,000 with a target annual bonus opportunity of 15%. Actual compensation will be determined based on a variety of factors, including the selected candidate's skills, experience, education, qualifications, and geographic location, as well as internal equity and business considerations. In addition to competitive pay, SunCoke Energy offers comprehensive benefits to employees and their families, including health care coverage, retirement benefits, life and disability insurance, paid time off, holidays, supplemental benefit programs, tuition reimbursement, employee assistance resources, and telemedicine. The company is currently seeking an experienced Welder / Fitter II for our facility in Reynoldsburg, OH. Specifically, the is responsible for all job activities required to support production processes. These activities include but are not limited to: fitting/adjusting parts, tacking, and MIG welding steel. Employee is responsible for visually inspecting parts. Welds components in all positions. Set up welding equipment. Ensure welds meet standards and specifications. Perform precision layout tasks and precisely fit together their structural parts and components. Read/work to engineered drawings and welding symbols. Perform shop mathematical calculations. Properly use personal protective equipment when required. Maintain regular attendance - have reliable means of transportation. Perform other tasks as assigned Qualifications Prior manufacturing experience is highly preferred. Any technical or vocational education/training in relation to skills listed below is also desirable. Must have the ability to pass a AWS D.1.1 3G vertical metal core pulse transfer weld qualification Must have advanced blueprint reading knowledge Knowledge of machine operation, cutting, sawing, drilling, and grinding parts is desirable Ability to use welding tools Forklifts and Overhead crane experience preferred (in-house training available) Team player - must be able to work with others Must have and maintain a high sense of urgency to meet and exceed all production goals Must have the ability to work alone and/or be a team leader Attentive to detail watching for material defects and any quality issues Physically capable of standing, walking, bending, pushing, pulling, reaching and twisting throughout shift Capable of repetitively lifting 25-50 lbs. Candidates must be flexible to work overtime as needed, which may include weekends and/or holidays Must be able to pass a background check and pre employment drug test. Work Environment While performing the duties of this job, the employee works in typical manufacturing environment with overhead cranes and forklifts. Overhead LED lights throughout the workspace create a bright workspace for employees to safely perform their work. Normally clean work environment where the process creates some grinding dust, heat/cold, fumes/odors, and vibration. Housekeeping is performed as needed throughout the day and at the end of each shift. The noise level in the work environment is normal to manufacturing processes with air tools, grinders, and other tools. Yearly audiometric testing is provided by the company to monitor areas for improvement. Non-climate-controlled facility in the summer, each work area is provided with fans to help keep cool. In the winter it is heated. jobs.description: 88421717 293531229 Requisition: 2026-196722 Pharmacist Job Locations US-OH-COLUMBUS ID 2026-196722 Line of Business PharMerica Position Type Full-Time Our Company PharMerica Overview PharMerica is hiring a full-time Pharmacist in Worthington! Join our closed-door pharmacy team where you'll work in a non-retail environment, dedicated to meeting the pharmaceutical needs of long-term care and senior living clients. If you're passionate about delivering exceptional service and high-quality care, we want to hear from you. Apply today and become part of a team committed to making a difference! Schedule: M-F: 10 hour shifts rotating between 7am-9:30pm Sa-Su: every 3rd weekend Benefits and perks for you! Medical, Dental, Vision insurance Health Savings & Flexible Spending Accounts (up to $5,000 for childcare) Tuition discounts & reimbursement 401(k) Company Paid Time Off Shift Differential DailyPay Pet Insurance Employee wellness and discount programs * Benefits may vary by employment status Responsibilities How YOU will benefit: Supportive team with room to work independently Ongoing training and career growth Advancement opportunities in a growing company Referral bonuses As a Pharmacist you will: Evaluate physician medication orders for drug appropriateness, correct dosage, potential drug interactions, and proper route of administration. Provide clinical recommendations to physicians and healthcare staff regarding medication therapy changes and optimizations. Maintain up-to-date patient/resident profiles, including medical history, lab results, and current medications (prescription, OTC, and home remedies). Ensure laboratory tests required for monitoring high-risk medications are appropriately ordered, reviewed, and communicated to the healthcare team. Collaborate with physicians, nurses, and other healthcare professionals to provide clinical and technical support. Document all communications and clinical interventions in the patient's medical record, including interactions with families and caregivers. Implement and enforce policies and procedures for the safe handling, dispensing, and clinical oversight/management of medications. Ensure compliance with all state and federal regulatory requirements related to pharmacy practice and medication management. Report medication-related errors and adverse drug events to the Pharmacy Manager as required. Educate and support clinical team and healthcare agency staff on safe and effective medication handling procedures. Perform other pharmacy-related tasks and responsibilities as assigned. Qualifications Qualifications Required: Bachelor's Degree in Pharmacy, Pharm D preferred One year experience in long term care desired License/Certification(s): current and valid pharmacist license in the state of practice Knowledge of drug therapy guidelines, medication safety practices, and regulatory standards (CMS, DEA, FDA). Proficiency in electronic medical records and pharmacy information systems Strong clinical judgement, and effective written and verbal communication *Position will be posted for a minimum of 7 business day About our Line of Business PharMerica, an affiliate of BrightSpring Health Services, delivers personalized pharmacy care through dedicated local teams, serving health care providers such as skilled nursing facilities, senior living communities, and hospitals. We also cater to individuals with behavioral needs, infusion therapy needs, seniors receiving in-home care, and patients with cancer. Operating long-term care, home infusion, and specialty pharmacies across the nation, we combine the personal touch of a neighborhood pharmacy with the resources of a national network. Our comprehensive solutions, backed by industry-leading technology and regulatory expertise, ensure accurate medication access, cost control, and compliance with best-in-class clinical standards. We are committed to enhancing resident health, reducing staff burdens, and supporting our clients' success. For more information, visit www.pharmerica.com. Follow us on Facebook, Twitter, and LinkedIn. Res-Care, Inc., dba BrightSpring Health Services (“ResCare”), is an Equal Opportunity Employer. jobs.description: 293531528 SUMMARY: The Senior Accountant, Grants and General Ledger is responsible for the accounting, administration and financial oversight of all College grants; primarily federal research grants and private grants from corporations and foundations. This position creates and monitors grant-related budgets. This position ensures timely and accurate grant reporting for all federal, state, local and non-government grants. The Senior Accountant, Grants and General Ledger oversees all grant-related cash receipts and the completion of related month-end, quarter-end and year-end journal entries for grant accounts. This position is also responsible for accounting for restricted scholarships. The position actively assists the Assistant Controller and AVP/Controller in the preparation of year-end financial statements in accordance with GAAP. ESSENTIAL DEPARTMENTAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Grants Accounting Supports pre-award grant activities by assisting with budget development, budget justifications, proposal transmittals, and grant budget submissions in collaboration with Associate Director of Sponsored Research. Manages all post-award grant administration, including financial accounting, expenditure monitoring, compliance oversight, and preparation of grant reports and quarterly and annual financial reports for the College's grant portfolio. Ensures compliance with federal, state, local, grantor, and institutional regulations and policies governing grants, including Uniform Guidance (2 CFR 200), and provides analysis and guidance on grant-related financial matters. Assists with indirect cost rate proposals and negotiations, Assists with grant, audit and regulatory reporting requirements, year-end financial statements (e.g., Uniform Guidance audit, financial compliance reviews, NSF Survey, SEFA, F&A proposal development), and the development and maintenance of grant policies and procedures. General Accounting Responsible for fixed asset accounting, including capitalization, depreciation, disposals, and reconciliations. Prepares and posts recurring journal entries, including departmental recharges, prepaid expense amortization and others as assigned. Supports month-end and year-end closing processes by ensuring all assigned journal entries, reconciliations, and accounting adjustments are completed accurately and within established deadlines. Actively assists the Assistant Controller and AVP/Controller in the preparation of year-end financial statements in accordance with GAAP and completion of the annual audit. Serves as back-up to Accounts Payable Manager. Assists with other duties and projects as assigned by the Associate Vice President & Controller or the Vice President for Finance and Business. Requirements: EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE: Minimum 3 years of experience in grants and general ledger accounting. Not-for-profit or higher education experience. Bachelor's degree in accounting, finance or related field; CPA or working toward CPA, Experience with Datatel's Colleague software Proven ability to understand grant applicant (PI) needs, requirements and requests to identify priorities. KNOWLEDGE SKILLS AND ABILITIES SKILLS: Critical thinking and problem-solving skills. Adept at navigating complex environments with evolving priorities and communication plans. Professional and interpersonal skills and an ability to communicate effectively in person, writing, and over the phone. KNOWLEDGE: Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals. Ability to compute rate, ratio, and percent. Must be detail-oriented with the ability to process a large amount of data with complete accuracy. Proficiency in Microsoft Office 365; Advanced Excel skills. ABILITIES: Must be able to keep information confidential. Acknowledge and comply with all departmental SOP, safety, and College requirements. Commitment to the College's mission, vision, and values

jobs.title: Director of the Freedman Center for Digital Scholarship (Librarian 3 Lead)
jobs.description: 293525588 OSITION OBJECTIVE Reporting to the Associate University Librarian for Creation and Curation Services, the Director of the Freedman Center for Digital Scholarship provides leadership, direction, and establishes priorities for all programs, services, and spaces associated with the Digital Scholarship department and the Freedman Center for Digital Scholarship. This includes responsibility for scholarly communication and open scholarship, text and data analysis, geographic information systems (GIS), research data management, and artificial intelligence services. The Director establishes priorities, operations, and services and implements assessment strategies to enable evidence-based planning and decision-making. They work collaboratively with all library areas and play a leadership role in library-wide planning and decision making as a member of the KSL Leadership Team. Expectations for Leadership Team members are outlined in the team charter. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS Provides creative and innovative leadership to the Digital Scholarship department and collaborates across the library and externally. Communicates effectively and employs general management theories and practices. Plans for the design and evaluation of policies, services, spaces, and programs. Effectively implements relevant policies, operations, and services with a user-centered approach. Implements change management when needed, develops operational procedures and policies, and advocates for all necessary staff and resources. Collects and analyzes data for evidence-based decision-making and planning. (25%) Collaboratively develops and implements strategies for the ongoing management, development, and maintenance of Case Western Reserve University¿s digital scholarship services. Leads a program that engages the campus community in initiatives that maximize the impact of the university¿s scholarship and knowledge resources. Explores new processes and systems to improve efficiency, assesses and evaluates activities, and keeps abreast of emerging trends and standards in digital scholarship and related fields. (15%) Directs the operations, staffing, technology, and programming of the Freedman Center for Digital Scholarship. Administers the continuous redevelopment of the Center¿s technology-enabled spaces, equipment, and services, and ensures that faculty, students, and staff are aware of its capabilities. Provides continuous outreach to the campus community about digital scholarship initiatives and services and integrates the Center into the library¿s collaborative service model. (12%) Provides leadership and direction for the scholarly communication program, collaboratively setting strategy and priorities for services that support researchers in copyright, publication strategy, and open access & open scholarship. This includes the university's institutional repository (Scholarly Commons), guiding its development, policies, promotion, and growth. (12%) Mentor, supervise, and develop library staff. Work with staff to set performance and development goals and objectives to encourage continuous improvement. Evaluate performance, recruit staff, and work to implement strategies for staff retention. (12%) As a member of the Kelvin Smith Library Leadership Team, actively contributes and engages in information sharing, ideation, library-wide planning, decision-making, and the development of the library's strategic framework. Implements all strategic objectives relevant to this position as a leader in the organization and within this area of focus. Specific Leadership Team guidelines are outlined in the team charter. (10%) Contributes to the library, the institution, and the profession through sustained and progressive scholarship, creative expression, and service at the state, regional, national, or international level; contributions will support the advancement of librarianship and increase service to the University and community. (7%) Cultivates a work environment that promotes and maintains an environment and culture of empathy, collaboration, and respect. (6%) NON-ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS Perform other duties as assigned. (1%) CONTACTS Department: Work with KSL leadership on policy and planning of resources, services, and operations. Work with department staff to ensure excellent service for the campus community. Frequently collaborate with staff on all levels of the organization to support the provision of library services, including colleagues in research services, collections, technology, and archives whose work intersects with digital scholarship. University: Consult regularly with faculty and university staff to ensure that client needs are considered and served, that services and planning are coordinated, and that policies are applied and implemented consistently. Partner with academic departments, the Office of Research, and University Technology on research computing, data management, and artificial intelligence initiatives. Collaborate with University Philanthropy to develop plans for continued philanthropic support of the Center. External: Participate in local, regional, and national organizations to maintain a network of information professionals which enhances our services and to stay abreast of trends and changes in the profession. Collaborate with colleagues in OhioLINK, consortia partners, and peer academic libraries, and work with vendors and platform providers to support digital scholarship technologies. Engage both existing and potential donors for continued philanthropic support of the Center. Students: Regular communication with student assistants in the department to provide assistance and information resources to support their education and research needs. SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES Supervise exempt staff and non-exempt staff, student employees, and temporary full- or part-time workers. QUALIFICATIONS Education: A Master's degree in Library/Information Science or an advanced degree in a related discipline plus six years of relevant library experience. Advanced educational credentials (second Master's degree, Ph.D.) preferred. Experience: Department heads must have sufficient experience and expertise in library leadership, management, and the work of a team/unit/department to serve as a supervisor, advisor, and mentor. Librarian level: Appointment to the level of Librarian 3 assumes that all requirements of the level will be met and sustained, that the individual will demonstrate continued and outstanding growth in the profession, and perform existing duties and responsibilities at the highest level. Librarian levels are outlined in the librarian assembly handbook. REQUIRED SKILLS Ability to make evidence-based decisions on a strategic basis; to engage in leadership activities in library, scholarly, and professional organizations; to exercise the highest level of professional judgment and provide evidence of longstanding leadership. Able to apply best practices; can use advanced techniques and technology to innovate; ability to perform or administer most complex or most specialized duties; communicate effectively; and employ general management theories and practices. Evidence of professional contributions (publishing, creative contributions, presentations, and/or professional service at the state, regional, national, or international level); notable contributions to advance librarianship and increased service to the University and community; keeps abreast of the role and application of trends for libraries in higher education. Clear awareness of current relevant best practices and standards for the development of digital scholarship services, including scholarly communication and open access, research data management, text and data analysis, GIS, digital publishing, and artificial intelligence. Record of success developing and promoting digital scholarship services, instruction, and programming to advance the success of faculty, staff, and students. Excellent communication, interpersonal, and customer service skills. Demonstrable collaborative management style and a commitment to exceptional user services. Demonstrated successful experience directing a technology-enabled space or center, including planning for equipment, software, staffing, and programming, and promoting its services to a campus community. The ability to engage staff in improvement and change, and proficiency in project management to initiate, facilitate, conclude, and evaluate projects with efficiency and effectiveness. Demonstrated ability to secure resources needed and to serve as a strong advocate to accomplish the mission of the library, including experience with grants, partnerships, or other external funding. An understanding of, and the ability to respond effectively to, changes in teaching, learning, and research, including current and emerging trends in research practice, instructional methods, and service assessment and outcomes measures. Ability to create and contribute to an environment of empathy, collaboration, and respect. Experience with supervising and mentoring staff including clear goal setting, regular feedback, and strong support for growth. Ability to demonstrate successful support, education, and advocacy for all students, aligned with the values, mission, and messaging of the university, while adhering to the staff policy on conflict of commitment and interest Ability to meet consistent attendance Ability to effectively interact with colleagues, supervisors, and customers face-to-face. Ability to cultivate an environment of empathy, collaboration, and respect WORKING CONDITIONS General office/library environment. This position is hybrid eligible in accordance with the university¿s hybrid program

jobs.description: 293531788 PURPOSE OF THIS POSITION The purpose of the role of Social Worker, Behavioral Health, is to assist in identifying, addressing, evaluating, and carrying out plans for behavioral health related needs for patients being treated in the Emergency Department, Medical Surgical Units, Intensive Care Units of BVH and Orchard Hall as needed. jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst - Distribution and Transportation
jobs.description: 88432411 293531864 Position Summary The Senior Data Analyst - Transportation & Distribution is responsible for transforming transportation, warehousing, and supply chain data into actionable insights that improve service, operational performance, and cost efficiency. This role develops and maintains KPIs, dashboards, scorecards, forecasting models, and advanced analytics to identify trends, uncover root causes, and drive data-driven decision making across the logistics network. The position partners closely with business leaders to evaluate optimization opportunities, build business cases, quantify savings, and support the implementation of process and network improvements. Additionally, the analyst plays a key role in logistics technology initiatives by supporting data integration, master data management, system implementations, and reporting solutions that enhance visibility and operational effectiveness. This is a hybrid role with the requirement of working onsite in Mentor, OH 3 days/week. Up to 15% domestic travel. This role is not eligible for Visa Sponsorship or H1B Transfer. What You'll do as a Senior Data Analyst, Distribution and Transportation Collaborate with Transportation and Distribution leaders to establish and maintain a multi-year analytics roadmap that aligns business priorities with data, reporting, forecasting, and optimization capabilities to drive measurable operational and financial results. Analyze transportation, distribution, warehousing, and logistics performance data to identify cost savings, service improvements, capacity constraints, and operational optimization opportunities. Develop actionable business cases and recommendations by executing Transportation RFQ's, evaluating network scenarios, transportation strategies, carrier performance, inventory positioning, and optimization opportunities. Present findings, recommendations, project updates, and realized business value to logistics leadership and key stakeholders, influencing strategic and operational decisions. Design, develop, and maintain executive dashboards, scorecards, and KPI's using industry data visualization tools like Tableau & Power BI ensuring all stakeholders and users are properly training to drive adoption of new tools Monitor key transportation and distribution performance indicators, investigate performance gaps, drill into underlying operational data, and partner with stakeholders to implement corrective actions. Partner with Transportation, Distribution, Procurement, Operations, Finance, and Supply Chain teams to evaluate and execute carrier sourcing events, transportation RFQs, network optimization initiatives, and continuous improvement projects. Serve as the functional expert for Transportation Management System (TMS), Warehouse Management System (WMS), dashboards, and logistics-related data sources, ensuring data integrity, master data governance, and reporting accuracy. Collaborate with IT, Data Engineering, and Business Intelligence teams to define data requirements, improve data accessibility, support system integrations, and implement scalable analytics solutions. Identify, investigate, and resolve data quality, data integrity, master data, and process issues that impact operational execution, reporting accuracy, and decision-making capabilities. Research emerging logistics technologies, market trends, transportation best practices, and analytical capabilities to continuously improve performance, visibility, and operational effectiveness. The Experience, Skills, and Abilities Needed Required Experience Bachelor's Degree. 5+ years of experience in transportation, distribution, logistics, supply chain analytics, operations analytics, or a related analytical role. 5+ years of experience gathering, analyzing, and interpreting large datasets to identify operational improvement opportunities, cost savings initiatives, and business insights. 3+ years of experience developing and maintaining dashboards, scorecards, KPI reporting, and data visualizations using tools such as Tableau, Power BI, or similar business intelligence platforms. Skills Advanced analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify trends, uncover root causes, evaluate operational performance, and develop data-driven recommendations. Strong transportation and distribution business acumen, including knowledge of freight operations, carrier management, warehousing, logistics networks, inventory flow, and supply chain processes. Expertise in business intelligence, reporting, and data visualization tools, including Tableau, Power BI, or similar platforms, with the ability to create actionable dashboards and executive-level scorecards. Proficiency in data analysis and data management, including data extraction, transformation, validation, cleansing, and interpretation from multiple data sources. Ability to translate complex data into actionable business insights and communicate findings effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Strong business case development and financial analysis skills, including ROI calculations, cost-benefit analysis, savings quantification, and opportunity prioritization. Strong presentation and communication skills, with the ability to influence leadership decisions through clear, concise, and compelling recommendations. Excellent stakeholder management and collaboration skills, with the ability to build relationships and partner effectively across Transportation, Distribution, Supply Chain, Operations, Procurement, Finance, and IT functions. Strong project management and organizational skills, including the ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and independently lead initiatives from concept through implementation. Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy, particularly when working with large datasets, KPI reporting, financial analyses, and operational recommendations. Ability to operate in a fast-paced, results-oriented environment, balancing strategic initiatives with day-to-day analytical support. What STERIS Offers We value our employees and are committed to providing a comprehensive benefits package that support your health, well-being, and financial future. Here is just a brief overview of what we offer: Market Competitive Pay. Extensive Paid Time Off (PTO) and 9 added Holidays. Excellent Healthcare, Dental and vision benefits. Long/Short Term Disability coverage. 401(k) with a company match. Maternity & Paternity Leave. Additional add-on benefits/discounts for programs such as Pet Insurance. Tuition Reimbursement and continued educations programs. Excellent opportunities for advancement in a stable long-term career. STERIS does not accept unsolicited resumes/CV's from individual recruiters or third-party recruiting agencies in response to job postings. #LI-BB1 Pay range for this opportunity is $85,000 - $110,000. This position is eligible for bonus participation. Minimum pay rates offered will comply with county/city minimums, if higher than range listed. Pay rates are based on a number of factors, including but not limited to local labor market costs, years of relevant experience, education, professional certifications, foreign language fluency, etc. STERIS offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits portfolio. Click here for a complete list of benefits:STERIS Benefits Open until position is filled. STERIS is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity to ensure that persons are recruited, hired, trained, transferred and promoted in all job groups regardless of race, color, religion, age, disability, national origin, citizenship status, military or veteran status, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth and related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, and any other category protected by federal, state or local law. We are not only committed to this policy by our status as a federal government contractor, but also we are strongly bound by the principle of equal employment opportunity. Applicants will receive fair and impartial consideration without regard to race, sex, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic data, or religion or other legally protected status.

jobs.description: 293531940 JOB RESPONSIBILITIES * Patient Transport- Perform skills as established by CCHMC Transport Team policy and procedure and guideline and the State of Ohio Board of EMS. Accept and comply with laws, regulations, rules, policies, and procedures. Operate Emergency Vehicles within applicable laws. Independently assess department needs and respond within Paramedic scope of practice according to the state EMS Board Division of EMS/Ohio Department of Public Safety. Assure crew, family, and patients adhere to safety requirements while in a moving vehicle. Ensure the work environment is organized, safe, accessible, effective, and efficient for patients, families, and coworkers. Report malfunctioning equipment and other environmental hazards immediately. Anticipate change in needs based on volume. This individual partners closely with Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Supply Chain, and Clinical Supply to ensure alignment, risk management, and successful achievement of program milestones. The successful candidate will have substantial experience supporting biologic development programs and drive CMC strategy for a late stage development asset. Facilitate team meetings, prepare agenda, publish meeting minutes, and ensure accountability for deliverables. Monitor project progress and proactively identify, assess, and mitigate risks. Coordinate CMC initiatives and activities, and partner with cross-functional teams to ensure readiness and timely delivery of technical documentation and regulatory commitments, and other CMC deliverables. Align with internal and external stakeholders to support production schedules, supply planning, and inventory management to ensure uninterrupted product availability. Additional duties assigned as needed. Education/Experience Requirements: Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Biology, Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related discipline required. Equivalent combination of education and applicable job experience may be considered MS, MBA, PhD, PharmD, or other advanced degree in a related discipline preferred 7+ years of relevant experience in biotechnology, pharmaceutical development, manufacturing, or technical operations 4+ years of project management experience supporting CMC, Technical Operations, Manufacturing, or Product Development programs Direct experience supporting biologic drug products, including CMC development, manufacturing, and lifecycle management activities Demonstrated experience managing complex cross-functional projects through clinical development and commercialization Experience supporting Biologics License Application (BLA) submissions and post-approval commitments is preferred Familiarity with GMP regulations, quality systems, and biologics manufacturing operations Knowledge of process validation, technology transfer, and commercial manufacturing operations for biologics Additional Skills/Experience: The ideal candidate will embody Travere's core values: Courage, Community Spirit, Patient Focus and Teamwork Driven, intelligent, passionate about making a difference for patients of risk mitigation strategies Ability to adapt to modification and changes to project plans, demonstrating flexibility to implement new strategies and tactics to accommodate these changes Team player and strong interpersonal and organizational skills and excellent verbal and written communication skills Excellent decision-making and collaboration skills with strong attention to detail Ability to travel 10% domestically and internationally All positions have an essential job function to be able to perform face to face work with colleagues and/or onsite in San Diego No role is expected to be 100% remote Total Rewards Offerings : Travere provides comprehensive total rewards offerings that demonstrate our commitment as a diverse, equitable, people-centric, and pay-for-performance organization. Benefits: Our benefits include premium health, financial, work-life and well-being offerings for eligible employees and dependents, wellness and employee support programs, life insurance, disability, retirement plans with employer match and generous paid time off. Compensation : Our competitive compensation package includes a combination of both cash compensation (base pay and short-term incentive) and long-term incentive compensation (company stock), designed to recognize, retain, and reward employees. Target Base Pay Range: $132,000.00 - $172,000.00 *This information is current as of the date of this posting and may be modified in the future. Protections for those who make complaints

If you make a complaint – or give information related to, or assist in, an investigation of a complaint – your identity will be kept confidential to the fullest extent possible under law and as necessary to investigate the complaint fairly.

Federal laws prohibit employers from retaliating (taking negative actions) against employees who report employment-related complaints. If you experience retaliation from an employer, notify the complaint representative.

common-questions.title: Common Questions
body: The first step to troubleshooting this issue:
Clear the cache & cookies from your internet browser.

The 'cache' is a tool used by your internet browser to speed up the time it takes for a page to load. However, sometimes it can cause a problem when websites are updated. Information saved in the cache may conflict with what's actually coded into the website. Clearing Cache and Cookies is a way you can be sure that any issues you may come across are actually something wrong with the website, rather than inconsistencies caused by using different browsers.
Keyboard Shortcut for Most Browsers
If you are using Internet Explorer, Edge, Google Chrome, or Mozilla Firefox you can quickly clear cache with a keyboard shortcut. With your browser window open:
Press Ctrl + Shift + Delete simultaneously on the keyboard to open the appropriate window.
Be sure to select all the options available to you: cache, cookies, any site data, site images, and files.
IMPORTANT:
After you clear the cache and cookies data, be sure to close/quit the browser window & restart it.
Google Chrome for Windows
Click the Tools menu (three dotted lines in the upper-right corner).
Select History.
Select Clear Browsing Data from the left-hand side. Set the Time Range set to All Time. Check-mark Cookies and other site data and Cached images and files and select Clear Data.
If on a Windows computer, close and re-open Chrome to save your changes. If on an Apple computer, go to the Chrome menu on the top menu bar and select Quit for the changes to take effect.
Google Chrome for iOS
Open Google Chrome on your iOS device.
Click on the menu toolbar in the bottom right corner.
Select Settings.
Select Privacy.
Select Cookies, Site Data, and Cached Images and Files. At the top, set the Time Range set to All Time.
Click Clear Browsing Data at the bottom of the screen.
Then confirm by clicking Clear Browsing Data again.
Mozilla Firefox
Click on the Tools bar.
Click on Options (On Mac, it's labeled Preferences).
On the menu to the left, select Privacy & Security.
Under the Cookies and Site Data option, click the "Clear Data..." button.
Select only the two options and hit clear now.
If on a Windows computer, close and re-open Firefox to save your changes. If on an Apple computer, go to the Firefox menu on the top menu bar and select Quit for the changes to take effect.
Microsoft Edge for Windows 10
Click the Tools menu (three dotted lines in the upper-right corner) then click the Settings menu.
Click Privacy, search, and services on the left-side menu.
Under the section Clear browsing data, Click Choose what to clear.
Select Cookies and other site data and Cached images and files.
Click Clear Now.
Close Microsoft Edge completely for your changes to take effect.
Internet Explorer for Windows
Click on the Settings menu in the upper-right corner.
Click Internet options.
Under the General tab on the upper-left-hand side, scroll down to Browsing history.
Select Delete...
Check the Temporary Internet files and website files, Cookies and website data, History, and Download History boxes.
Select Delete.
Close Internet Explorer and reopen it for changes to take effect.
Safari for iOS
Go to the Settings app on your device.
Scroll down to the Safari menu.
Scroll down and select Clear History and Website Data.
A pop-up will come up verifying that you want to clear the History and Data. Select Clear History and Data.
The button for Clear History and Website Data will turn gray when cache and cookies have been successfully cleared.
Safari (macOS)
Click on Safari on the top menu bar.
Click Preferences.
Click the Privacy tab.
Click Manage Website Data...
Click Remove All.
Click Remove Now.
Go to the Safari menu on the top menu bar.
Select Quit to close Safari and save your changes.
How do I create a free account?
Creating a free account is easy.
If you are an adult Job Seeker, from the Home Page, click the "Log In/Sign Up" button at the top, right-hand corner.
All users of OhioMeansJobs.com
must
have an
OH|ID
account to create an account with OhioMeansJobs.com. Click the "Go to OH|ID" button to either create an OH|ID or log in to your existing OH|ID account.
After you sign in with your OH|ID, you will be brought back to OhioMeansJobs.com to create your OhioMeansJobs.com account. Click the "New to OhioMeansJobs? Register Here," link
Enter your contact information and then click "Next."
Note:
You must enter at least the first three digits of your zip code and choose from the drop down list in order to populate the City and State/Province fields. These two fields cannot be manually entered
Enter information about your Military Service, any security clearance you may have and your current employment status.
Enter information about your Target Job Title, Current Work Status, Work Experience and Career Level.
Enter your highest degree attained and whether or not you are currently a student or intern.

Enter any Workplace Accommodations you may need, your Willingness to Relocate, where you may be willing to relocate to, your willingness to travel for the job, and maximum miles you're willing to commute.
Your registration is complete and you can begin your job search, upload your resume or visit your Dashboard to view a number of different job search and professional development tools.
How do I change my password?
NOTE: These instructions do NOT pertain to the
Office
of Unemployment initial temporary passwords.
If you are a Job Seeker, from the Home Page, click the "My Profile" button at the top, right-hand corner.
If you are a K-12 Student, click "For Students". Then click the "My Profile" button.
Once you've signed in, you should see your name on the left-hand side, toward the top of the screen.
Underneath your name, you should see a hyperlink "Edit Your Account"
At the top of the screen, under "Log in Information", you should see your email address.
Click, "Change Password" and follow the instructions.
Click, "Update Account" to submit.
Password Requirements
8 to 20 characters long.
At least one number.
One symbol (excluding ' @ - " <).
A combination of upper and lower case characters.
To reset a password while not logged in:
Click My Profile.
Click forgot password.
In the box that opens enter the email on the account.
Click submit.
A reset email will be generated to that email account.
Access your email account and open the email from omjnoreply@monster.com.
Click the hyperlink in it to open the webpage to make a new password.
To reset a password by answering your security question:
Click My Profile
Click forgot password
In the box that opens asking for an email, do not enter an email instead below the submit button click on the sentence that says “
I am an Ohio Program Participant, and I don’t have an email
It will then ask the security question, Answer correctly and you will then be prompted to set a new password.
Note: The answers are case sensitive.
Where can I change my account settings?
Make changes to your account settings from your profile.
If you are a Job Seeker, from the Home Page, click the "My Profile" button at the top, right-hand corner.
If you are a K-12 Student, click "For Students". Then click the "My Profile" button.
Once you've signed in, you should see your name on the left-hand side, toward the top of the screen.
Underneath your name, you should see a hyperlink "Edit Your Account"
From here, you can edit your contact information, military service, career & employment information, and more!
How can I find scholarship information?
OhioMeansJobs.com aggregates over 1 million available scholarships.
Get the education you need or desire. Finding scholarship information is an important step in going from a dream to a reality.
If you are a Job Seeker, from the Home Page, click the "My Profile" button at the top of the screen.
If you are a K-12 Student, click "For Students". Then click the "My Profile" button.
Once you've signed in, scroll toward the bottom of the screen and find,"Scholarships I'm Interested In".
Click, "View Scholarships".
From here, you can see the scholarships you've saved.
Above the column headers, click, "Return to Scholarship Search" to find new scholarship opportunities.
From here, you can search by Intended Major, your grade level, zip code, GPA, and college.
Be sure to save your search criteria for future use!
How can I get help preparing for my exams?
OhioMeansJobs.com is committed to helping you reach your full potential.
Our free, virtual classroom gives you access to over 1,000 digital pieces of training and tutorials.
If you are a Job Seeker, from the Home Page, click the "My Profile" button in the top, right-hand corner.
If you are a K-12 Student, click "For Students". Then click the "My Profile" button.
Find the "Assessments & Training" section, in the left-hand column.
Click, "View Test".
Click, "Visit Online Training Center".
From here, you have the option to select a wide variety of training and tutorials.
NOTE: The ONLY way to save your work is by logging into your free account. If you do not log-in, your progress will not be saved.
Tips For Success
Read the instructions before you begin. Once you feel comfortable, click "Start Test".
Take charge of your in-progress tests and tutorials from "My Assessments", found in the blue header of the "LearningExpress" page.
High School Students
Prepare for the SAT, ACT, CLEP, and other entrance exams. Find an extensive list of Advanced Preparation (AP) exam subjects. Or brush up on your general test-taking skills.
College Students
Get ready for pre-professional and graduate school entrance exams. Find content to get you ready for the DAT, GMAT, GRE, LSAT, MAT, MCAT, & PCAT graduate school exams.
Professional Certifications

Prepare to take career exams from many industries. Find tests for the following careers: Allied Health, Air Traffic Controller, Civil Service, Commercial Driver's License (CDL), Cosmetology, Culinary Arts, Electrician, Emergency Medical Services, Firefighter, Green Careers, Homeland Security, Law Enforcement, Legal, Military, Nursing, Plumbing, Real Estate, Social Work, & Teaching.

Curious about any of these professions? Click any profession, then select "Learn More Guidance" next to the job title. Read an overview of the position and how to best use the practice tests and tutorials available for this job.
English as a Second Language Exam
Prepare for the TOEFL iBT® or IELTS™ to demonstrate your English language proficiency.
Adult Learning

Prepare for High School Equivalency Exams, including Spanish Language content. Improve your basic skills. Demonstrate your computer literacy. Build your financial literacy and create a foundation for life-long success.
U.S. Citizenship Exam
Use our online training materials to your advantage.
This free and easy to use tool can help launch you into the job you've always wanted.
How can I manage my resume?
You can store multiple resumes on OhioMeansJobs.com
Keep your resume at the top of employer’s search results to maximize your chances of landing that next career opportunity.
If you are a Job Seeker, from the Home Page, click the "My Profile" button at the top, right-hand corner.
If you are a K-12 Student, click "For Students. Then click the "My Profile" button.
Find the "Resumes" section, in the right-hand column.
Click, "Manage Resumes".
From here, you have the option to Create a Resume OR Upload an Existing Resume.
You must complete all the required fields, marked with a red asterisk (
When you create a new resume, you can "Select Resume Sections" to format a resume that best suits the job you are applying for.
For each resume you add, you have additional functionality available.
In the "Status" column, be sure to click "Inactive".
This opens up a dialog box.
Select, "Active", if you want your resume to be found by employers and recruiters.
When you select, "Active" you will be offered additional options.
Click "Update" to confirm your selections.
IMPORTANT TO NOTE
Only one resume can be active at a time
. When you make a resume status "active" if you have already set a different resume to "active" the resume status of your first resume will be automatically changed to "inactive".
We recommend that you
click the "active" link on your resume every 30 days
. This maximizes the chances of your resume being seen by an employer. The "last updated date" gives you verification of successful renewal.
Diversity Candidates:

OhioMeansJobs.com is used by thousands of companies that recognize the benefits of diversity in the workplace. They are actively recruiting qualified applicants from diverse backgrounds including race, gender, 50+ workers, disability status, and lifestyle preference. By selecting the Diversity checkbox option you will make your resume public to employers searching the diversity and inclusion resume databases. You can change this setting at any time.
Confidential Resume

: By selecting this, employers who are interested in your resume will still be able to contact you via a confidential OMJ email address, but they will not be able to see the personal information that you have provided on this site. You can view job listings and decide whether or not to respond.
If you apply online, the information you've marked as confidential WILL be included so that the employer can contact you.
If you choose to hide your contact information, current company, and references, you must ALSO remove this information from your uploaded resume.
Are there events in my area?
More Than A Job Search Site
OhioMeansJobs.com is committed to supporting Job Seekers, Employers, & Ohio's communities.
From the home page, in the top header, click "News & Events".
At the top of the page, click "Find Events".
Here, you can search by county, from the right-hand column.
Click an event name to read the description.
Click, "Register for this Event" to add the event to your OhioMeansJobs.com calendar.
Verify your personal information and click, "Register Now".
Find job fairs, workshops, and other events going on in your community. Register for events that sound good to you. Keep track of everything with the calendar available in your profile.
NOTE: You must be signed in to your profile before you can register for an event or job fair. You do not need to register for job fairs, just add the event to your profile.
Can I get some additional help in my job search?
From any page, click the "My Profile" button found in the top, right-hand corner.
Find the "Programs I'm Interested In, Ohio-based Employment Programs" section, in the left-hand column.
Click "Search Programs".
In the right column, click the checkboxes to sort and filter.
Click "Update" to populate results.
Search & filter, by group:
Dislocated
Employed but looking
High school youth
Special population
Students
Targeted population
Unemployed
Universal population
Veterans
Youth
Youth offenders
You can also search by “Services Offered”:
Assessments
Basic skills training
Business services & recruitment
Career exploration, Job matching, & Job placement
Continuing education, professional development
Co-ops, Internship – related training, Apprenticeships
Education & training
Licensing and testing for careers (testing fees)
Remedial education & academic intervention
Stipend

Click the launch button to search for employment programs near you.

How can I add an event to My Calendar?
Calendar
Get directions and set reminders to attend virtual or in-person events you've added to your calendar.
To access your calendar:
Log in to your account.
Click “Tasks.”
Scroll down to “Your Calendar.”  Click “My Calendar.”
To add an event:
Log in to your account.
Click “Tasks.”
Scroll down to “Your Calendar.”  Click “Find Events.”
Search for all events by selecting a county. Click on a county name to select that county.
Filter the results to a specific type of event by clicking on the event type.
Available events for the county selected will be displayed.  Click on the event title for additional information on the event or to register.
To register, click “Register for This Event.”
Complete the required fields.  Then click “Register Now.”
To print event details, click “Print.”
Click “Calendar” to go to your calendar.
Click an event title to:
Delete the event.
Add a note.
View the event details.
Click “Delete,” then click “Cancel This Registration” to cancel the event and remove it from your calendar.
Click “Back to Events” to continue searching for events.
To view registrations, click “View My Registrations.”
Events you are currently registered for will be displayed.
Click “Past” to see your event registration history.
Are there events in my area?
More Than A Job Search Site
OhioMeansJobs.com is committed to supporting Job Seekers, Employers, & Ohio's communities.
From the home page, in the top header, click "News & Events".
At the top of the page, click "Find Events".
Here, you can search by county, from the right-hand column.
Click an event name to read the description.
Click, "Register for this Event" to add the event to your OhioMeansJobs.com calendar.
Verify your personal information and click, "Register Now".
Find job fairs, workshops, and other events going on in your community. Register for events that sound good to you. Keep track of everything with the calendar available in your profile.
NOTE: You must be signed in to your profile before you can register for an event or job fair. You do not need to register for job fairs, just add the event to your profile.
How can I be sure that I'm in the right career?
The career profile is a quiz to find occupations that match your interests.
The questions ask about your likes and dislikes. They take about 30 minutes to complete.  There are no right or wrong answers.
You should take this quiz if:
You are not sure what kind of job you'd like.
You want to change careers.
You need to choose a field of study.
Your responses will measure how much the words below describe you:
Artistic
Conventional
Enterprising
Investigative
Realistic
Social
How to Take the Career Profile
1.    Log in to your OhioMeansJobs.com account (if you’re not already logged in).
2.    From any page, click your name or “My Profile” in the top right corner.
3.    Then click on “Dashboard.”
Click the “Career” tab in the middle of your dashboard.
Scroll down to the “Career Profile” section.
Click “View Careers.”
7. Click "Get Started."
8. Read the instructions and click "START."
9. You will be shown a list of 60 activities. Indicate how much you would like or dislike each one.
10. When you finish answering all the questions on a screen, click “Next” to move to the next          page. (If you missed any questions, the “Next” button won’t appear.)
11. Click “GET SCORE” after you answer all 60 questions.
12. You will receive 6 scores, one for each of the following personality factors: Artistic,     Conventional, Enterprising, Investigative, Realistic, and Social.
How to Find Occupations That Match Your Interests
1.  Click the blue "View Occupations" button at the bottom.
2.  Click on the job titles to learn more.
3.  To save an occupation to your dashboard for future reference, click the "Save" button at the top     of the job description.
How to Compare Occupations
Check the boxes for at least two job titles.
Click “Compare.”
A pop-up window will open comparing the occupations selected.
How to Retake the Career Profile
Click the “Career” tab in the middle of your dashboard.
Scroll down to the “Career Profile” section.
Click “Edit” on the far right.
You will see your most recent answers.
Make any changes you’d like.
When you finish answering all the questions on a screen, click “Next” to move to the next page. (If you missed any questions, the “Next” button won’t appear.)
Click “GET SCORE” after you answer all 60 questions.
How can I find the Career Pathway for an occupation?
Career Pathway

Career pathways are typical paths by which an individual might reach employment in a certain occupation. While they are by no means the only way to become employed in each occupation, they offer a general guideline. While these career pathways are organized by their primary industry, it should also be noted that career pathways and occupations can be found across multiple industries.
Click “For Job Seekers.”
Under “Practice Your Skills,” click “Career Path.”
Select a Career Cluster.  Click the arrow to begin exploring.
You will see occupations found in that Career Cluster organized by a Career Pathway.  A Career Pathway will show the education and the training you need to work in that occupation.
Click “Learn More” to learn more about that occupation including pay, education, skills needed, Ohio Employment Trends, and more.
Click the plus sign (+) on the occupation to save the Career Pathway.
You will be directed to the OH|ID log-in page.  From here, you can log in to your OH|ID account.  Or you can create an account if you don't already have one.
You will then be routed back to Career Pathway in your OhioMeansJobs.com account. A message will be displayed that the occupation has been saved. The plus sign will now be a check mark.
Click the “Career” tab from your Dashboard to access your saved Career Pathways.
Can I get some additional help in my job search?
From any page, click the "My Profile" button found in the top, right-hand corner.
Find the "Programs I'm Interested In, Ohio-based Employment Programs" section, in the left-hand column.
Click "Search Programs".
In the right column, click the checkboxes to sort and filter.
Click "Update" to populate results.
Search & filter, by group:
Dislocated
Employed but looking
High school youth
Special population
Students
Targeted population
Unemployed
Universal population
Veterans
Youth
Youth offenders
You can also search by “Services Offered”:
Assessments
Basic skills training
Business services & recruitment
Career exploration, Job matching, & Job placement
Continuing education, professional development
Co-ops, Internship – related training, Apprenticeships
Education & training
Licensing and testing for careers (testing fees)
Remedial education & academic intervention
Stipend
Supportive services
Tax credits
Click the launch button to search for employment programs near you.
How do I use School Finder?

You can use the School Finder tool to explore your higher education options.  The tool lets you search, compare, and save schools best suited to your career goals.  Here's how to use the School Finder toolkit:
Log in to your account.
Under " Your Tasks," click “Go” under “Schools I’m Interested In.”
Select the type of school that you want to attend.
For a quick match, click “Start.”
You can search by city or zip code.
Start to type your city’s name. When the full name appears, click on it.
If your city doesn't appear in the list of options, select the city nearest you.
Start to type your zip code. When the zip code appears, click on it.
Then click “NEXT.”
Select the type of school that you want to attend.
Then click “NEXT.”
Select up to five areas of study.  Click “MY SCHOOL MATCHES.”
To add additional search criteria, Click “Advanced School Search.”
Select additional filters to the left by clicking on them.
To search using key words, start to type in a school name or a location. When the full name appears, click on it.
Then click “GO.”
There are options to download, print, or save at the top and bottom of the page.
How do I use the Lifestyle Calculator to determine my target salary?
Ohio Lifestyle Calculator
The lifestyle calculator can be used to help determine your target salary based on your location and estimated expenses.
Here's how to calculate your target salary:
Click “For Job Seekers.”
Under “Practice Your Skills,” click “Career Skills.”
Under “To
p
Tools,” click the arrow to see more options.
Click “Target Salary Calculator.”
Click “Launch.”
Click “Ohio Lifestyle Calculator.”
Select a region by clicking on a city name to the left or by clicking a location on the map.
For each question, select expenses that fit your lifestyle
by clicking on the boxes that apply. Then click “Next.”
After you have answered all 12 questions, click “Next: Results.”
You will see target numbers for “Gross Annual Target Salary,” Net Annual Target Salary,” and “Target Hourly Rate.”
To see job postings that pay your target salary, click “View Jobs.”
OR type in keywords (such as "doctor" or "build houses") and  click “View Occupations.” This will give you more information about careers in a specific field that pay your target salary.
Back on the "Adding it All Up" results page, click “Save To Profile,” to save your results.
You will be directed to the OH-ID log-in page.  From here, you can log in to your OH-ID account.  If you don't already have an account, you can create one.
You will then be routed back to your OhioMeansJobs.com account.
You can find saved “Lifestyle Calculator” results by clicking the “Career” tab on your Dashboard.
Click “Recalculate” to make changes.
How do I complete a Veteran Questionnaire?
How to Complete the Veteran Questionnaire
Receive specialized support with your employment and training needs by completing the Veteran Questionnaire.
Click, "For Job Seekers."
Under “Build Your Career,” click, “Military Service.”
Click, “Read More.”
To the right, under “For More Information,” click, “Veteran Questionnaire.”
Click, “FILL -IN.”
Complete the questionnaire.
Save to your computer and email it to
ohiovetsfirst@jfs.ohio.gov
How can I map my military skills?
Get help finding civilian jobs that match your military skills.
This information will empower you to build your resume and search for a great civilian career.
Click "For Job Seekers."
Under “Build Your Career,” click “Military Service.”
Scroll down.  Click “Military Skills Translator.”
Click “Launch.”
Select your branch of service from the drop-down menu.
Then enter your military job title. When you start typing, options will appear.
Click “Search Jobs Now.”
You will get a list of civilian jobs that match your military experience.
Click on a job posting to learn more about it. You also can use the job titles listed as key words on your resume. This will make it easier for employers to find you and to understand your skills.
The Military Skills Translator is also accessible from the "Military Service Career Center" landing page.
Scroll down and click, “Career Resources & Benefits.”
Click “Military Skills Translator.”
How do I receive help navigating post military transition?
OhioMeansJobs.com Veteran Transition Plan
Military affiliated users can take advantage of the Veteran Transition Plan in their profile to:
Help successfully navigate their post military transition.
Select tasks and measure progress on post military transition goals.
Access links to Military.com articles and OhioMeansJobs.com tools that provide information to help complete each task.
Getting Started
Using OhioMeansJobs.com is easy, and it can help you find a new job quickly.
From any page, click the "Log In/Sign Up" button in the top right corner.
Click the blue button that says, “Go to OH|ID.” You can find it near the bottom of the page, on the left. You will then be prompted to log in to your OH|ID account or create one.
After you enter your OH|ID and password, you will be routed back to OhioMeansJobs.com.
Click “sign in here” to log in to an existing account.
Click “Register Here” to create an OhioMeansJobs account.
Update Your Information
The Veteran Transition Plan will show on your account profile if you select that you are an Active-Duty Military member and your year to transition is within 1 year of the current date.
How do I find resources for transitioning from Military Service?
Transitioning From Military Service
Transitioning service members
can access a variety of free employment services at both
OhioMeansJobs.com
and the state’s OhioMeansJobs Centers.
When military members, their spouses, and veterans register for a free account on
OhioMeansJobs.com

they’re prompted to answer a brief questionnaire asking if they’d like to be contacted by an employment specialist. In addition, the resumes of veterans are designated with a red and blue “V,” and the resumes of military spouses are designated with a red and blue “S,” to make them stand out to military-friendly employers.
Veterans and their eligible spouses get priority of service at both
OhioMeansJobs.com

and the state’s OhioMeansJobs Centers. Both online and in-person services are available, tailored to individuals' needs.  Individuals can access as many or as few of these services as they'd like, on their own or with the help of an employment specialist.
Click "For Job Seekers."
Under “Build Your Career,” click “Military Service.”
Scroll down and click, “Transitioning from Military Service.”

The federal Transition Assistance Program is designed to help transitioning service members and their spouses prepare for their next step in civilian life. To access the program’s online courses, click
TAP self-paced online courses
” under
Transition Assistance Program (TAP).
To learn about other federal resources, click the other links on this page.
Click “Launch” to learn more about the federal Transition Assistance Program.
To learn about additional resources for members and their
families
, click “
Military OneSource
” under "For More Information."
Where can I find Labor Market Information?
The Ohio Department of Job & Family Services maintains
Ohio's Labor Market Information
(LMI).
Need details about jobs? Use our
specialized search tools
From the occupational search page, you can find jobs by industry, education, keyword, or salary. You can only search by one criterion at a time.
Start with the Industry drop-down. Select Manufacturing and click, "Go".
From the Manufacturing landing page, you can view a definition of the industry.
In the left-hand column, you can navigate to “fun facts” and other information.
Click on Labor Market Information to learn about:
Employment projections for manufacturing.
The number of manufacturing business establishments in Ohio
The education needed for careers in manufacturing.
The average age of workers in manufacturing, & more.
View a snapshot of the industry to find out:
How many jobs were posted?
The salary, education, certifications, and skills needed for the industry.
Top employers and occupations with the most job ads.
Select Industry Careers to narrow down your interest.
A list of occupations will appear, with in-demand occupations listed at the top.
Ohio has identified in-demand occupations based on wage, the projected number of openings, and expected industry growth.
Click a job title to find out even more.
At the top of the page, you’ll find a brief description of the job, occupations with similar job duties, and related industries.
The Work Activities section lists typical job duties, employment trends, the outlook for the job, education, and income information.

We hope this information has been helpful. Remember to check back often and search as many occupations as you’d like. This information is updated frequently to help you find your first, next, or a better job!
How do I register an account as a SNAP/TANF Recipient?
Food and Cash Assistance Guide
Have you been assigned activities in
OhioMeansJobs.com
Important Benefit Information
To continue receiving food and/or cash assistance benefits:
You must complete the job search and training activities that your caseworker assigned.
You must complete them by the due dates.
If you have questions, please contact your caseworker at your county department of job and family services.  For your county agency's contact information, see the local
Agencies Directory
Step 1: Create an account on OhioMeansJobs.com
Click “For Job Seekers” and then click “Learn About Benefits.”
Scroll down and click “SNAP/TANF Work Requirements.”
Click “Launch” to the right.
If you already have an OHID account, log in.
If you don't yet have an OHID account, you can create one now.
When prompted, click "Create Account."  Y
ou will need:
An email address where you can get a one-time PIN and confirmation email.
Your legal first and last names.
Your date of birth.
A mobile phone number to use as an account recovery option.
You will be prompted to create a username and password. Requirements will be provided.
You will then be routed back to OhioMeansJobs.com.
If you already have an OhioMeansJobs.com account, enter your credentials and click “Sign in.”
If you don't yet have an OhioMeansJobs.com account, click "Register Here."
You will be prompted to answer a few questions about yourself.
NOTE: If you would like to change your email address, first name, or last name, that must be done within OHID.
When finished, click "Next".
Great! You have successfully set up your account with OhioMeansJobs.com!
Step 2: Create or upload a resume

Your resume contains your detailed work history, education, and skill set. If you don’t have a resume, OhioMeansJobs.com can help you create one. You can even choose to have your resume rated so you can see how to make it better. Whether you upload an existing resume or build a new one,
be sure to mark it “Active” so employers will be able to see it
Resumes
You are required to create or upload an active resume on OhioMeansJobs.com.
You can store multiple resumes in your OhioMeansJobs.com dashboard. To access your dashboard, just click on your name in the top right corner of any page and then select “Dashboard.”
To create or upload a resume, follow these steps:
From your dashboard, click on "Tasks."
In the box titled “Create or upload your own active resume,” click "Go."
Choose “Create a Resume” OR “Upload an Existing Resume.”
Complete all the required fields. They will be marked with a red asterisk
To upload an existing resume, first it must be saved to your computer. You can’t upload a resume using a phone or other mobile device. You also can’t transfer resumes from other websites.
When you create a new resume, you can "Select Resume Sections" to choose the kind of resume you want and how you want it to be formatted.
Select one resume to be “Active.”
Only one resume at a time can be active. This will allow employers and recruiters to see it.
To change a resume status from inactive to active, or from active to inactive:
Check the appropriate box in the “Status” column.
Click “Update” to confirm your selection.
IMPORTANT
Whenever you make a resume "Active," if you have any other resumes saved, they will be marked "Inactive."
We recommend that
you click the "Active" link on your resume every 30 days
. This will improve the chances that employers will see it. The "last updated date" will change to today’s date every time you click “Active.”
Diversity Candidates:

Thousands of employers recognize the benefits of diversity in the workplace and actively recruit qualified applicants from diverse backgrounds. By selecting the “Diversity” checkbox, you’ll make your resume stand out to these employers. You can change this setting at any time.
Confidential Resume

: If you select this, employers who are interested in your resume will still be able to contact you via a confidential OhioMeansJobs.com email address. However, they will not be able to see the personal information that you have provided on this site. You can view job listings and decide whether to respond.
If you apply online, the information you've marked as confidential WILL be included so that the employer can contact you.
If you choose to hide your contact information, current company, and references, you must ALSO remove this information from your uploaded resume.
Step 3: Apply for jobs and track your job searches
Your caseworker will determine the number of jobs you must apply for. It’s important that you track your job search so you can prove that you completed the required activities.
IMPORTANT
: Save each job that you apply for to your dashboard and mark it as “Applied.”
Step 4: Assessments and training
Your caseworker may assign assessments and/or trainings for you to complete by given dates. Whenever you complete an assessment or training, your caseworker will receive a
report
Remember:
Be sure to document your work-search efforts.
Continue to visit OhioMeansJobs.com to research careers and search for jobs.
