OMJ (OhioMeansJobs)
Steps to register for an Employer account
Go to
https://www.ohiomeansjobs.com/
Click the “For Employers” link
Click the “Log In/Sign Up” button in the upper right corner
Click the “Go to OH|ID” button on the Account Action Required page.
Sign in with your OHID account, if you do not have one click “Create Account”.
On the Employer Transition Page, scroll to the bottom of the page and select the “Create New Account” button.
Click “Select One” and click “I have a FEIN and a tax withholding account number.”
Employers should NOT choose “I have an OMJ Center FEIN.” This will only work for OhioMeansJobs Centers who are attempting to register their staff.
Enter and confirm your company’s FEIN and Ohio Tax Withholding Number without dashes, then click “Continue.”
If you do not know your company’s FEIN/Tax ID number, you can either contact your payroll department or check your W2 for that information.
If your Tax Withholding Number is 9 digits, just enter the first 8 digits
Enter your registration information.
When you enter your zip code, your city will be automatically populated for you.
Phone number and email should be for the individual user, not the company’s general contact information.
Password must be 8-20 characters, must include at least 1 letter and number or symbol and should not have either your first or last name, username or parts of your email address incorporated into it.
This password is for your employer record and separate from your OHID password.
Click the “Create Account” button.
You will then see the Employer Dashboard where you can view your most recent job postings, search resumes, post new jobs and review Ohio-based employment programs.
I need help locating the FEIN or State Tax ID for my company.
Why do I need these ID numbers?

OhioMeansJobs.com requires you to provide your state and federal ID numbers to create an account. This allows us to verify your company and provide the highest level of information security and privacy to Ohio’s citizens and businesses.
Your Federal Employer ID Number (EIN or FEIN) identifies your employer to the IRS.
Your Tax Withholding ID identifies your employer to the State of Ohio.
Where can I find these ID numbers?

You can easily find this information on your own. As an employee of your company, each year you are provided with a Form W-2. This Wage and Tax Statement includes your employer’s Federal and State ID numbers.
From your W2:
You can find the FEIN in Box B. It is a 9-digit number with a dash between the first two digits. It should look like this: 00-3456789
You can find the Employer’s State ID in Box 15. It is an 8-digit number that begins with 51, 52, 53, or 54.
Don't have a W2?
Reach out to your company’s payroll department or processor. They should be able to provide you with both numbers.
Are you a third-party representative?

You will need to contact the company you are representing. They will need to provide you with their Federal Employer ID Number (FEIN) and Ohio Tax Withholding ID if you wish to use OhioMeansJobs.com on their behalf.
Need more help?
Contact the
Ohio Department of Taxation
at (888) 405-4039, option 3. Be sure to verify that you have
the required information
available before you call.
Confirm your company is registered with the
Ohio Business Gateway
How can I post a job?
Go to
https://www.ohiomeansjobs.com/
Click the “For Employers” link
Click the “Log In/Sign Up” button in the upper right corner
Click the “Go to OH|ID” button on the Account Action Required page.
Sign in with your OHID account, if you do not have one click “Create Account”.
You will then see the Employer Dashboard where you can view your most recent job postings, search resumes, post new jobs and review Ohio-based employment programs. Select the Post a Job “Go” button.
Posting Shortcuts

You can reuse a job posting you've saved in your Hiring Library as a template. This saves time by avoiding retyping the same details. To access your Hiring Library, use the link for Hiring Library in the drop down above your name in the top-right corner of the screen.
Job Type -
Choose the type of job you're posting:
Regular job
Federal contractor role
Internship
Apprenticeship
Agricultural work (H-2A, FLC)
Job Details -
Fill in the basic info about the job:
Fields with a red asterisk (*) must be filled out.
The more details you provide, the better chance you'll find the right candidates.
You can create a reference code to help organize your search. This system won’t create one for you.
Job Description -
You can either upload a document or type the job description directly:
To upload, use a file in .doc, .docx, .txt, or .rtf format and click ‘Browse’.
After selecting your file, finish the rest of the page and click ‘Continue’ or ‘Save for Later’ to upload.
To type or paste your description, use the text box and formatting toolbar.
Want to start fresh? Click “Clear” in the editor.
When done, click ‘Continue’ or ‘Save for Later’ to save your work.
Company Info -
Enter your company name and industry. If you want to keep your company name private, check the box below the field.
How Candidates Apply -
By default, applicants apply online, and their resumes are tracked automatically. The email listed here is pulled from your account:
You can change this email if needed.
You can also choose other ways to apply, up to two methods total like email, fax, or direct contact.
If you choose email, you’ll see a second field to add another address for receiving resumes.
Licenses or Certifications -
List any required certifications (e.g., teaching, paraprofessional, tech, driver’s license). Adding details helps attract qualified candidates.
Skills-Based Hiring -
If you're a TalentNEO Skills Based Partner, you agree to use skill scores when reviewing applicants:
TalentNEO helps partners by suggesting skill scores, updating job descriptions to focus on skills, and improving hiring workflows.
NAICS Code -
This is a standard code used by federal agencies to classify businesses. It helps with collecting and analyzing economic data.
WorkKeys® -
WorkKeys® is a system that helps you assess job skills and build a strong workforce.
Posting Dates -
Set when your job post goes live and when it expires:
Default expiration is 30 days, but you can adjust it.
Maximum posting time is 90 days.
Check the job category and update it if needed, this helps your post show up in the right searches.
How can I  manage a job posting?
Getting Started
Logging In
From the Home Page top navigation, Click “For Employers”.
Then click the “
” button, in the top right corner.
Managing Jobs
IMPORTANT
: Changes to job postings can take 4-6 hours to be reflected on the live site.
Once you've signed in, click "My Jobs" in the header, on the right-hand side of the screen.
Then click, "Manage Jobs".
In the left-hand menu, under "Views", you will find a list of Posting categories. Click the links to navigate.
You can refine the jobs that appear in each list using the edit filters.
Find the number of postings associated with the job, the posting dates (active and expired), and job seeker activity, including the number of views, clicks, and applies.
Clicks recognize Jobseeker activities such as saving the job to the backpack or applying to the job.
Clicks are counted when a job seeker clicks on any active link you included during the creation of the job.
Job Actions
You can change the content and status of an individual job (and its postings) using the Action links.
Actions include edit, copy, archive, renew, and expire.
Manage Candidates
From the top header, click "My Candidates"
Then click, "Manage Candidates".
Candidates who are included in the selected folder are displayed on this screen.
Adjust your candidate list view (brief or expanded information) using the icons located above the list.
You can refine the candidates that appear in the list using the filters available to the right of the candidate list.
To view an individual candidate's profile, click the candidate's name.
Candidate Actions
Manage individual or multiple candidate profiles using the Actions menus. Actions include:
Copying and forwarding a profile
Adding a note
Blocking candidates (a “blocked” icon will be added to the candidate's profile in folders and subsequent job search results).
Job Posting ID Number
To easily find a listing, use the keyword search to identify your postings by ID number.
Pre-Screening Questionnaire

For applicants coming through OhioMeansJobs.com, you can elect that they complete a pre-screening questionnaire. You can also send an auto-reply letter when someone finishes their application. Just like job postings saved to the Hiring Library, questionnaires can be saved and shared within your entire company or kept private to your individual account.
Sample questions are available for you to import for many different occupations.
You can edit these to tailor them to your exact needs.
Use a few different types of questions:
Multiple Choice
Yes or No
Open text field.
Send different auto-reply letters, based on the applicant's responses.

This means, that you can send a letter to candidates who meet your hiring criteria that their resume has been received and you are looking forward to reviewing it. Job seekers appreciate this courtesy and it affirms to them that their materials have been delivered appropriately.
How can I search for resumes and find candidates?
Go to
https://www.ohiomeansjobs.com/
Click the “For Employers” link
Click the “Log In/Sign Up” button in the upper right corner
Click the “Go to OH|ID” button on the Account Action Required page.
Sign in with your OHID account, if you do not have one click “Create Account”.

You will then see the Employer Dashboard where you can view your most recent job postings, search resumes, post new jobs and review Ohio-based employment programs. Select the Find Candidates “Go” button.

On the Resume Search Tool, you can look for candidates by Job Title, Keywords, or Location. You must fill in at least one of these before searching. Every search you run is automatically saved under “My Saved Searches.”
When you click Search, you’ll go to the results page. This page has three sections:
Search Criteria (your filters)
Results (list of candidates)
Resume Preview (quick look at a candidate’s resume)
In the Search Criteria section, you can change your search by adding, removing, or switching fields by clicking “Manage Fields”
In the Results section, each candidate appears on a card with:
Match Percentage (green number): Shows how closely the candidate fits your search.
Name
Tags (icons next to the name):
Red, White, & Blue
“V” = Veteran of the U.S. Armed Forces
Red & Blue
“S” = Spouse of a Veteran
“AO” = Interested in an apprenticeship
Blue
Circle with colors = Earned the OhioMeansJobs Readiness Seal in high school
Current/Most Recent Job Title and Location
Updated Date: When the resume was last changed
Current Job: Most recent job title and company
Top Skills: Key skills pulled from the resume
The Resume Preview section shows a summary of the candidate’s resume. Switch to the Resume tab to see the full uploaded document.
In the upper
right corner of the preview, you can take actions:
Favorite: Save as a candidate you want to track
Forward Resume: Email it to someone
Download: Get a copy of the resume
Send Email: Contact the candidate directly
Add to Folder: Save in a folder for easy access later
Under the three
dot menu, you’ll find more options:
Skip: Hide this resume for the session
Add Note: Write comments (visible only to you/your company)
Block Communication: Stop interacting with this resume for the session
Report Issue: Flag a resume that looks fake or problematic (sent to Help Desk)
Add to Compare: Select up to 5 resumes to view side
by
side
How do I manage user accounts?
Managing User Accounts as an Administrator
What is the difference between the user types?
OhioMeansJobs Standard User: can access resumes and post jobs.
OhioMeansJobs Administrator: can access resumes, post jobs, and manage other standard user accounts.
Edit a User's Account
Log in to your employer account.
Click “Administrator.”
3. Click “Edit.”
4. Check the box by the user you wish to update.
5. Click “Actions” to the right.
6. Click “View/Edit.”
You can then update the following:
Status-Make an account active or inactive.
Role-Make an account an Administrator or Standard user.
Update user information such as email, address, and phone number.
Reset a user password.
Click “Save” to save any changes.
Disable a User's Account
Check the box by the user you wish to update.
Click “Actions” to the right.
Click “Disable.”
Click “Continue.”
Reset a User's Password
There are 3 ways to reset a user password
Select the user.
Top left, under “Actions”, click “Reset Password.”
Or check the box by the user you wish to update.
Click “Actions” to the right.
Click “Reset password.”
Or check the box by the user you wish to update.
Click “Actions” to the right.
Click “View/Edit.”
Click “Reset Password.”
Where can I find admins for my company?
Sign In
From the Home Page top navigation, Click “For Employers”.
Then click the “
” button, in the top right corner.
Once you've signed in to your recruiter account, click the gear icon next to your name.
Then click, Account Settings".
In your Account Profile, click the "View Company Admins" hyperlink.
Here, you should see a list of the names, email addresses, and phone numbers for your company's administrators.
Tasks for Company Administrators.
Getting Started
From the Home Page top navigation, Click “For Employers”.
Then click the “
” button, in the top right corner.
Promote an Account from User to Administrator
Click Manage
Click OMJ Users
Search by name or email address, click the correct name to select.
In the User Type field select, "OMJ_Administrator".
Click, "Save".
What is the difference between the user types?
OMJ_User: can only access resumes.
OMJ_Administrator can access resumes and manage other user's accounts.
Reset a User's Password
Click Manage
Click OMJ Users
Search by name or email address, click the correct name to select.
Click, "Reset User Password".
You should see a message confirming, "Password Reset Successful"
Inactivate a User's Account
Click Manage
Click OMJ Users
Search by name or email address, click the correct name to select.
In the Current Status field, change the status from "Active" to "Inactive".
Click, "Save".
Military Friendly Employer Designation
In the top right corner, next to your name, click the Gear Icon
From the dropdown box, Click "Account Settings".
Here you can update the Military Friendly designation for your company.
How can I update my company information?
Company information that is publically available on OhioMeansJobs.com is aggregated from search engine data.
Google has provided comprehensive support for businesses, to help you
keep your information accurate and up-to-date
Clicking the hyperlink will navigate you away from OhioMeansJobs.com.
How do I designate our company as Military Friendly?
Want to thank a veteran? Hire one.

Ohio is proud to be called home by more than 700,000 veterans and military service members — the 5th largest veteran population in the United States. OhioMeansJobs.com gives you access to our database of millions of resumes for free.  In addition, you can add your organization’s name to Ohio’s
Military-Friendly Employer Registry
to make it easier for current and former military members and their spouses to see your job openings.
Not sure if your company is listed as a military-friendly employer?
If you are the administrator of your organization’s OhioMeansJobs.com account, just follow these steps to check:
Log in to your administrator account.
Click your name upper right.
Click “Company Profile.”
Click “Edit."
Scroll to “Military-Friendly Employer.”
If the “Military-Friendly Employer” option is set to “No,” and if your organization would like to be on the list, click the drop-down and select “Yes.”
After you click “Yes,” click the link below it that says, “Click to select Military-Friendly Employer activities.”
On the next screen, check all the boxes that apply to your organization.
Click “Continue.”
At the bottom of the next screen, click “Save.”
Thank you for supporting Ohio’s military service members and their families!
What is Veteran Priority of Service?
Ohio veterans have an edge...
Federal law requires veterans to receive priority of service in
all
employment and training programs funded by the U.S. Department of Labor
At OhioMeansJobs.com, this means employers see qualified veterans' resumes first when they search for candidates.
To search for veteran candidates:
Log in to your employer account
Click “Dashboard.”
Under “Find Candidates” click “Go."
Set “Search Settings” to “Boolean Search Field.”
In the search field, e
nter your search criteria using words like "AND" or "NOT" to
specify what you're looking for-for
example
"Sales AND Marketing NOT Audit."  You can enter
such things as a job title, skills, or industry.
Enter the location and radius you'd like to search.
Click the magnifying glass to start your search.
Resumes will a
ppear
for you to review.
The resumes that most closely match your key words will appear first.  If the percentage of match is the same, veterans' resumes will appear at the top.  Veterans' resumes have a blue and red V icon.
To add additional search criteria, such as “Security Clearance,” follow these steps:
Click “Manage Fields.”
Click the plus sign by the field you wish to add. It will then appear to the right under “Active Search Fields.”
Click “Close.”
The field will then appear to the left where you can add additional filters.
To search only veterans' resumes:
To view only veterans' resumes, search the key word “Veteran,” your location, and a smaller radius.
What is Military Spouse designation?
Free Career Services for Military Spouses

Military spouses can be a great addition to any employer’s workforce. Their resumes might show that they’ve had many different jobs, because of frequent relocations, but this only proves their adaptability and depth of work experience. They’ve served their nation selflessly, and hiring them is one small way to give back.
On
OhioMeansJobs.com
, you can easily find the resumes of military spouses. They have a red and blue “S” by their names.
Military Spouse Employment Partnership
Military Spouse Employment Partnership (MSEP)
is a U.S. Department of Defense Military OneSource employer program. The MSEP program gives employers access to a unique and talented group of professionals – military spouses.
Military-Friendly Employer Registry
Ohio has more than 8,000 employers listed in its “Military-Friendly Employer Registry.” To see if your organization is listed as a Military-Friendly Employer, follow these steps:
Click the "My Profile" icon to create a free account or sign in.
Once your account has been created, in the top right next to your name, click the gear icon.
Then click “Account Settings.”
Next to your account profile, click “Edit.”
Here you will see your military-friendly status. If your organization’s status need to change, click the "View Company Admins" hyperlink.
Ask your organization’s OhioMeansJobs.com administrator to change your status, if needed.

education.title: Help for Students and Education
body: OMJ (OhioMeansJobs)
How to Register a K-12 account?
Creating a free account is easy.
If you are a student in grades K-12, click "For Students.” Then click “Students Home.”
Click “Log In/Sign Up” in the upper right corner.
Click the blue button that says “Go to OH|ID.” You can find it near the bottom of the page, on the left.
If you already have an OH|ID:
Use your OH|ID credentials to log in to your OH|ID account.
Respond to the prompts to secure your account and verify your identity.
You will be returned to OhioMeansJobs.com website.
If you have not yet created an OH|ID:
Enter the email address that you plan to use for your K12 student OhioMeansJobs.com account.  Then click “Verify.”
You will receive an email containing your six-digit verification code. The email will be sent from the following email address:
DONOTREPLY-EnterpriseIdentity@ohio.gov.

It may take several minutes for you to receive this email. If it seems to be taking a long time, please check your spam folder. If you don't receive the email, please have your schools information technology team whitelist the
DONOTREPLY-EnterpriseIdentity@ohio.gov
address.
Enter this six-digit verification code in the pop-up message on the registration page. Then click “Verify.”
Complete the next five steps.
Click “Create Account.”
You will receive a registration email when your new account is ready. Do not attempt to log in to your OH|ID until you receive this email.
Log in to your OH|ID account and respond to the prompts to secure your account and verify your identity.
You will be returned to OhioMeansJobs.com website.
Click “sign in here” if you already have an account.
Enter your original OMJ K-12 login information.
Click “Register Here” if you need to create an account. You will be prompted to answer a few questions about yourself. Then click "Create Account."
Registering a new account
Answer the questions about yourself to create the correct type of account.
Now answer the questions about your school.
Start to type your school’s name. When the full name appears, click on it.

Enter the year you expect to graduate. (If you are not a student, this question will not appear. If you are a student, you must provide your expected graduation date, or the “next” button will not appear.)
To allow your teacher to view what you do on the website, click “Yes” under “Sharing your activity.”
Congratulations!  You have successfully registered an account on OhioMeansJobs.com.
How do I take the Guided Tour?
OhioMeansJobs Guided Tour
Not sure where to start? Need help navigating OhioMeansJobs?
Take this guided tour to discover what OhioMeansJobs has to offer.
Click “For Students.”  Then click “Student’s Home.”
Click “Student’s Guided Tour.”
If you already have a K12 account, click “I already Have an Account.”  If not, click EITHER “1. Register with OhioMeansJobs K-12” OR “Let’s Go” to create an account.
Once logged in you will be prompted to start the activity you last left off on, in chronological order.  Tasks completed will have a line thru the task name.
Click “Let’s Go” to start where you left off.  You can also click the arrow on any activity tile to do that activity.
There are 8 tasks in the Guided Tour.
Register a K-12 account. Will take one to OHID to log in then back to register an OhioMeansJobs K12 account.  If you already have an account, it will take you to your account dashboard.
Complete the Career Cluster Inventory.
Create a Career Plan.
Build a Budget or Use the Lifestyle Calculator.
Tools for College and Career Readiness. (Assessments and Training Section.)
Build or upload your resume.
Search for jobs.
Review your Profile Strength.
How do I complete the Career Cluster Inventory?
Career Cluster Inventory
Answer some questions about your likes and dislikes to find careers that match your interests.
Your responses will measure how much the words below describe you:
Artistic
Conventional
Enterprising
Investigative
Realistic
Social
Click “For Students.”
Under “Explore Careers,” click “Learn About Career Types.”
Scroll down.  Click “Career Cluster Inventory.”
Click “Launch.”
Click “Get Started.”
Click “Start.”
Select the answer that best describes how you feel about each activity or job.
Note: To save your answers as you go, click "NEXT" on the bottom of each page.  To keep your scores, on the final page click "Get Scores" and then click "SAVE."
When you're done with each page, click “NEXT” to proceed.
If "NEXT" does not appear, you missed a question.
After you answer all 80 questions, click “GET SCORES.”
Scroll down to “What next?”
Click “SAVE” to keep your results.
You will be directed to the OH|ID log-in page.  From here, you can log in to your OH|ID account.  Or you can create an
account
if you don't already have one.
After you log in to your OH|ID account you will be routed back to your account Dashboard on OhioMeansJobs.com
To see your saved scores:
Scroll down to “Your Tasks.”
After “Career Cluster Inventory,” click "Go."
To view career suggestions based on your interests:
Click “OCCUPATION SEARCH.”
Choose the drop-down options that you would like to search.
Scroll to “Career Cluster Search.” Select a Career Cluster result.  Click “Go.”
You will see occupations organized by Career Pathway.  A Career Pathway will show the education and the training  you need to work in that occupation.
How can I find Readiness Seal information?
Readiness Seal
Are you a motivated high-school student? If so, earn the OhioMeansJobs-Readiness Seal to show employers you have skills they need!
How can you earn the Readiness Seal?
Ask

three trusted adults, or mentors, to certify your skills. They could be teachers, coaches, club advisors, youth group leaders, job or internship supervisors, or others. You’re probably already doing the work you need to do to earn the seal.
How can you get started?

Just download the validation form. (See below for where to find it.) Then find your three mentors and give them the mentor resources. Tell your school counselor and principal that you’re working to earn the OhioMeansJobs-Readiness Seal.
Where can you find the validation form?
In OhioMeansJobs.com, c
lick the top “For Students” tab.
Click “Student’s Learning Kit.”
To obtain information on the Readiness Seal:
Click the Launch button to get started!
Click, “For Students.”  Then click, “Student’s Learning Kit.”
Scroll down. Click “Readiness Seal.”
Under “Additional Downloads,” click “Get the validation form from the Ohio Department of Education.”
Where can you find more information?
In OhioMeansJobs.com, c
lick the top “For Students” tab.
Click “Student’s Learning Kit.”
Scroll down. Click “Readiness Seal.”
Click the blue “Launch” button.
Click “Print Guidelines” to download the OhioMeansJobs-Readiness Seal Guidelines.
How can I find scholarship information?
OhioMeansJobs.com aggregates over 1 million available scholarships.
Get the education you need or desire. Finding scholarship information is an important step in going from a dream to a reality.
If you are a Job Seeker, from the Home Page, click the "My Profile" button at the top of the screen.
If you are a K-12 Student, click "For Students". Then click the "My Profile" button.
Once you've signed in, scroll toward the bottom of the screen and find,"Scholarships I'm Interested In".
Click, "View Scholarships".
From here, you can see the scholarships you've saved.
Above the column headers, click, "Return to Scholarship Search" to find new scholarship opportunities.
From here, you can search by Intended Major, your grade level, zip code, GPA, and college.
Be sure to save your search criteria for future use!
How can I get help preparing for my exams?
OhioMeansJobs.com is committed to helping you reach your full potential.
Our free, virtual classroom gives you access to over 1,000 digital pieces of training and tutorials.
If you are a Job Seeker, from the Home Page, click the "My Profile" button in the top, right-hand corner.
If you are a K-12 Student, click "For Students". Then click the "My Profile" button.
Find the "Assessments & Training" section, in the left-hand column.
Click, "View Test".
Click, "Visit Online Training Center".
From here, you have the option to select a wide variety of training and tutorials.
NOTE: The ONLY way to save your work is by logging into your free account. If you do not log-in, your progress will not be saved.
Tips For Success
Read the instructions before you begin. Once you feel comfortable, click "Start Test".
Take charge of your in-progress tests and tutorials from "My Assessments", found in the blue header of the "LearningExpress" page.
High School Students
Prepare for the SAT, ACT, CLEP, and other entrance exams. Find an extensive list of Advanced Preparation (AP) exam subjects. Or brush up on your general test-taking skills.
College Students
Get ready for pre-professional and graduate school entrance exams. Find content to get you ready for the DAT, GMAT, GRE, LSAT, MAT, MCAT, & PCAT graduate school exams.
Professional Certifications

Prepare to take career exams from many industries. Find tests for the following careers: Allied Health, Air Traffic Controller, Civil Service, Commercial Driver's License (CDL), Cosmetology, Culinary Arts, Electrician, Emergency Medical Services, Firefighter, Green Careers, Homeland Security, Law Enforcement, Legal, Military, Nursing, Plumbing, Real Estate, Social Work, & Teaching.

Curious about any of these professions? Click any profession, then select "Learn More Guidance" next to the job title. Read an overview of the position and how to best use the practice tests and tutorials available for this job.
English as a Second Language Exam
Prepare for the TOEFL iBT® or IELTS™ to demonstrate your English language proficiency.
Adult Learning

Prepare for High School Equivalency Exams, including Spanish Language content. Improve your basic skills. Demonstrate your computer literacy. Build your financial literacy and create a foundation for life-long success.
U.S. Citizenship Exam
Use our online training materials to your advantage.
This free and easy to use tool can help launch you into the job you've always wanted.
